newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but well off session highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but well off session highs.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended firmer on Friday, but prices drifted off highs after buying subsided and scattered speculative profit-taking and trade sales emerged in the afternoon, dealers said.

Local short-covering and speculative buying pushed the spot May contract to a high $1,429 a tonne, just shy of resistance at $1,432. May delivery ended at $1,412, up $1 on the day. May reached a low of $1,394.
Active July finished $7 firmer, at $1,451, after trading from $1,465 to $1,433. The outer months gained $3 to $10 lower.
Cocoa prices slipped at the outset, but quickly recovered with trade interest in the May/July spread helping lift prices off lows. May/July ended at 39, from 33 at the close on Thursday.

News that some Ivorian exporter agents said exporters were short cocoa for immediate shipment helped steady prices, traders said. However, other agents noted this represented only a temporary squeeze rather than a broader supply problem.
Talk that a U.K.-based commodity analyst estimated the 1996/97 Ivory Coast mid-crop cocoa harvest (April-Sept) would come in at 115,000 tonnes was also viewed as supportive, traders said.

Estimates for the mid-crop have ranged between 100,000 and 160,000 tonnes, with recent beneficial rains putting many recent forecasts toward the higher end of the range. During the 1996/95 bumper season, the Ivorian mid-crop came in at some 200,000 tonnes.
Additionally, traders were also encouraged by both the London and the U.S. markets' ability to hold steady after sharp sell-offs early this week.

After the close Friday, the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 8 showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 2,130 lots, to 16,537, while non-commercial short positions increased by 65 lots, to 3,371 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 48 lots, to 58,587 lots and commercial short fell by 2,449 lots, to 80,853 lots.
Nonreportable long positions declined by 1,780 lots, to 19,316 lots, while nonreportable short positions fell by 1,478 lots, to 10,216 lots.
Traders said the report, which showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 22,266 lots, was within expectations.

Some traders said market was likely to trade sideways with continued liquidation and rollover ahead of May first notice day on April 17 capping any upturn. They noted that while May open interest continued to decline on Thursday, falling 2,019 lots, it still remained relatively high at 13,577 lots.
Volume on the exchange reached an estimated 12,464 lots, up from Thursday's official tally of 10,167 lots.
